messages:
maya: Kicking off calibration-set selection for the upcoming quant bakeoff (GPTQ / AWQ / INT8 / FP8). Goal = representative coverage + targeted edge cases so deltas are meaningful.

sam: +1. I'd start with task-family stratification: chat, summarization, code, QA, math, translation. Keep counts per family.

liam: Also stratify by length buckets: <32, 32-128, 128-512, >512 tokens. Aim for >=200 examples per bucket for the final set, smaller for quick runs.

natalie: Domain coverage note: sample from product docs, support transcripts, public web, OSS code. Avoid PII but keep domain artifacts (tables, code fences, long lists).

maya: Token distribution: ensure rare-token / unicode cases, lots of punctuation, repeated tokens, and long-prefix KV-cache scenarios. Include synthetic adversarial prompts (unclosed braces, malformed JSON).

sam: Quick numbers: small sanity set = 2k examples (for dev GPTQ/awq tuning), final calibration = 10k+ examples. For GPTQ use fixed-window 512 tokens during calibration; AWQ benefits from mixed-length examples.

liam: Draft sampling command (pseudo):
```
# stratified_sample.py
# usage: python stratified_sample.py --src datasets/meta-index.parquet --out calib.csv --per-task 500 --buckets 4
# picks proportional by task, then by length bucket, enforces domain quotas
```

natalie: Prompt curation checklist: include instruction style, few-shot examples, tool calls (function signatures + args), role switches, chain-of-thought seeds, and stop-sequence edgecases. Also include templated variants to test prompt sensitivity.

eval-bot: Quick sanity run finished: baseline (fp16) vs gptq-int8 on 2k sample => avg perplexity delta +0.6%, exact-match aggregate drop 0.8%, code-EM drop 1.4%. Detailed csv at s3://redwood-evals/quant/results/quicksanity/1759002374.csv

maya: Thanks. Propose pass/fail thresholds for bakeoff: ppl delta <1.5% (overall), EM drop <1.5% for NL tasks, <1.0% for code/compile tests. Anything outside triggers closer analysis and per-task whitelisting.

sam: Also flag qualitative failures: hallucinations on knowledge tasks, broken tool-call JSON, or truncation on long-context prompts. Those need targeted golden prompts.

liam: For deployment profiles: hosted API -> prefer AWQ-int8 for cost-first with canary rollback; dedicated -> keep a GPTQ-int8 variant for strict latency SLAs; private on-prem -> offer FP8 or INT8 depending on customer GPU. Must include automatic fallback policy in rollout config.

natalie: We'll annotate each calibration example with metadata: task_family, domain, length_bucket, rare_token_flag, seed_prompt_template. That makes per-slice regression analysis easier.

maya: Where to land artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/quant/calib/{date}/ and PR with index CSV, sampling script, and README describing strategy. Include a small eval harness config for the bakeoff.

sam: I'll spin up the stratified sampler PR and add unit tests for quotas and no-PII filter. Tagging @liam for review.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: INF-4723 - "quant calib sampling script + bakeoff config" (owner: sam). ETA: next week.

sam: will post a short thread with sampling outputs and a random 50-example preview for human review.

maya: Cool, thanks everyone. We'll use the 2k quicksanity for the nightly runs and the 10k as final pre-release gate.

natalie: One last thing: include a handful (~50) of localization/emoji-heavy prompts to catch tokenization edge cases.

sam: noted, will add to sampler.
